text: Microsoft's Recall feature became a privacy scandal in 2024 because, despite claims that data was encrypted, security researchers demonstrated that screenshots were stored unencrypted (in plaintext) in a local SQLite database [Source: ev-1]. This meant sensitive information visible on the screen—such as passwords and private messages—was captured by default and accessible to any process running under the user's account [Source: ev-1]. The feature had been announced on May 20, 2024, at Microsoft Build as an AI "memory" tool that took frequent screenshots of the user's screen [Source: ev-1]. In response, the relaunched version is now opt-in (default OFF), requires Windows Hello authentication and presence detection to access the timeline, and excludes incognito or DRM content [Source: ev-1]. This revised, privacy-focused version reached general availability on Copilot+ PCs in 2025 [Source: ev-1].
